label: context.reference
description: Arrange event-driven work by inspecting its condition, receiving task and result path.
text:
Use this guide for work that should happen later, repeatedly or in response to an event. Establish the intended action, the condition that should start it and where the result belongs. Use the existing conversation to resolve the intended behavior.

Inspect relevant existing triggers and the interfaces available in this installation (`inspect_authoring` returns the clean `interfaces.world` / `interfaces.system` map with bound runs and the `ee_instances` tree, separate from per-run private copies). A time schedule, an HTTP/file change or condition, an incoming message or another event may need different owners. Reuse an arrangement that fits. When it does not, inspect the current contract and source of the relevant owner and adapt or implement the capability within your grant.

A trigger is an interface folder with its own condition; when the condition holds it sends an artifact, and every checkpoint that pins the folder receives it. A requirement-free checkpoint is a standing route, so one binding receives every firing without re-authoring the run.

Two reusable JSON-configured sensor families cover most recurring attention without writing driver code:
- Time and quiet triggers (`copy_of: "world_cron"`): `interface.json`, `life.json` and an `activation.json` whose `cron_life` config holds only the schedule (`interval_seconds`, `cron`, `due_at` or `inactivity`); it sends `cron.current_time`. A disabled time folder that no run binds is a template.
- External observation triggers (`copy_of: "world_watch"`): `interface.json`, `life.json` (copied from `world_watch`; for local `file` watches set `allow_network: false` and declare the watched parent directory in `authority.read_paths`), and `probe.json` declaring an `http` (`GET`/`HEAD` poll), `file` (local file poll), or `webhook` (local/tunnelled HTTP push listener defaulting to `127.0.0.1` with constant-time `hmac_sha256`/`bearer`/`header` verification; `source.auth` always uses `token_file` or `env`, never inline secrets) source, extraction (`text`/`json` with `json_pointer`/`status`), and trigger (`on_change`, `on_match` with predicates and optional recovery, or `always`, plus `notify_on_error` and `hold_while_working`). It sends `watch.event` (or the configured `label`) with `untrusted_external_data: true`.
Bind either sensor folder into the run that should act, as an external input of a new run or of the current one.

Keep triggers discoverable in the client's Triggers view. It lists `cron_life` activations and external event sources with an active receiving checkpoint: World sensors (`interface_type: world`, `role: sensor`, `direction: inbound` or `bidirectional`) and connected applications whose `private_config.task_input_labels` declares what a task receives unprompted, such as incoming mail or messages. Choose a readable source identity and a receiving-task title that describes the action. The client derives their presence from these declarations; there is no separate UI registration. Preserve the source's actual classification; if its arrangement is not represented, identify the missing client support.

Trace the condition through to its consumer. Find the receiving run, the provider or tool that performs the work, and the route that delivers the result. Look for related inputs, outputs, retained state or future templates that must change together. The task-authoring guide describes provider frontier ownership; other owners define their own contracts. Copying a few visible checkpoints does not establish the complete connection.

Check the requested timing against the installed interface's timezone, repetition and next due condition. Use the owner's configuration result for setup and the receiving result when execution is part of the task.

Explain what will happen, under what condition and where the result will appear. Describe the trigger's current state, including whether it is armed or has fired. Save reusable configuration guidance with its applicable conditions.

Choose a time trigger's period for what it does: a six-hour period only when that rhythm is intended; ordinary recurring work needs a shorter one.
